cases.scenario: Load A and load B were separate van loads and separate charges. The app’s first description omits its load letter. One receipt image includes both payment lines.
One intake clerk created a record with no amount while waiting for the mill’s bill. Finance later entered the settled bill for the same intake ticket.
Travel and interpretation were separately reimbursed lines on one facilitator invoice. Each record captures one line rather than the invoice total.
The first amount was based on the uncleaned intake weight. After stones and chaff were removed, the one batch was invoiced on its lower net weight.

right.description: Wheat milling, cleaned net weight 920 kg.

cases.scenario: Only sixteen bags were dispatched according to stores. A replacement ticket was printed when the original got wet; the app records have different ticket references because the reprint prefix was transcribed.
An amber resin drum was exchanged for red at no additional charge. One entry was made before the exchange and edited to red; the other came from the exchange note. There was only one charge.
The supplier replaced a receipt that had the wrong tax total. Both uploads describe the same twelve-pair collection; the app amounts retain the old and corrected totals.
The fruit and seeds required different chambers. They were separately billed, and their job descriptions retain the temperatures and cargo types.
Washing and reproofing were separately charged stages for the same ten jackets. The combined invoice is attached to both entries, and each amount is one line charge.
The workshop says certificate LL-22 was voided and replaced after a clerical error, with no extra fee. The submissions include the voided sheet and replacement sheet.
Two laboratories used the same commercial room but rented separate allocated shelves. Their expense locations name the receiving laboratories, and one combined statement was attached.
The driver’s cash receipt was entered first. An office record from the card terminal report appears later, but the driver says cash was returned when the card payment succeeded.
The briefing sheets and stock labels were placed by unrelated teams and paid separately. Their descriptions are accurate; no common reference or document is available.
The base wash and stain treatment were charged separately on the same bill. The left record was intended to capture the base wash, but its description was shortened incorrectly.
The initial issue was charged on one invoice. The replenishment arrived two weeks later under another invoice; its app reference accidentally repeats the first invoice number.

left.description: Steel-toe boots, twelve pairs, initial issue.

cases.scenario: Drying and milling were billed as two different services on the same consignment. The two records each quote the consignment reference.
Two replacement poles were bought from separate shops after both teams broke theirs. The wording and prices happen to match; the paper receipts stayed with the teams.
Each desk had its own interpreter for the same afternoon. The agency used one programme reference, but the desk locations remain in the app.
The sharpener serviced a batch of ten knives in June and another batch of ten in September. Both were legitimate charges under the kitchen’s standing service agreement.
The facility charged unloading separately from shelf-space rental. The two line charges appear on the same consignment invoice.
The deposit and balance were separate instalments of the same order, not repeated claims for either instalment. The two instalments have equal amounts and the contract scan is shared.
The first shipment was collected and a replacement shipment arrived a day later for a fresh seven-day rental. The shipper’s standing booking code was copied into both references.

left.description: Locker hire, fruit shipment, seven days.

right.description: Locker hire, fruit shipment, seven days.

cases.scenario: Eight defective pairs were returned and exchanged without a new charge. The return credit and replacement invoice each show the full positive merchandise value in the app.
Separate planting crews each ordered 200 seedlings and paid separately. Their delivery locations are retained, while the nursery used one project-wide reference.
The mill has two handwritten tickets whose serials differ by one digit. The operator cannot tell whether one was rewritten after a spill or whether two batches were processed.
The reservation has no amount. A later cash charge might be its settlement, but the reference is absent and two produce events were held that weekend.
The agency accepted one payment but issued a new receipt when the terminal’s first print was unreadable. Both entries quote the payment ID, and the workshop had one contracted language service.
The written translation and spoken discussion were separate services ordered for the same consultation. Their distinct descriptions and separate references remain in the records.
The parks survey and drainage survey placed identical orders a month apart. The purchase descriptions were copied from the catalogue.
A volunteer’s note lists a can opener and peeler. Another note lists a can opener, peeler and whisk; neither states whether it is a combined summary or a separate purchase.
The recorded reference is a standing order covering monthly solvent collections. These notes concern September and October collections, each paid separately.

right.description: Solvent for cleaning line sprayer, four tins.

cases.scenario: The emailed invoice was reissued after the buyer name was corrected. One charge and one four-saw collection appear in the tool register.
The revision note refers to ticket L-884, but the original record quotes L-848. The handwritten digits on both documents are unclear, and no collection date survived.
The Tuesday and Wednesday briefs used the same cover wording and cost the same. They were printed and paid on separate days.

The supplier split one sixty-spatula invoice between two separately funded teams. These records each claim a different thirty-spatula allocation of equal value; the invoice scan and reference are shared.
One purchase was for the station island and one for the market island. The work diaries establish this, but neither location was copied into the app.
A power outage triggered a service credit, reducing the one chamber bill. The revised bill and original bill were both submitted, without a refund entry.
One voucher may cover a volunteer’s portion of a pooled order. The other may be the entire pooled purchase, but the coordinator has no contribution ledger or itemised receipt.
The crew returned to the counter the following morning for another six pails after using the first batch. Both cash slips were kept; no numbers were transcribed.
The gate teams each received twenty pairs from two separately paid deliveries. The deliveries used a shared requisition number.

An identical second pack was purchased after the opening week when the first set was insufficient. There were two separate payments and two receipt files.
The breakfast kitchen and evening kitchen separately bought twelve ladles at the same shop. Each purchase has a different till transaction, but identical catalogue text.

One collection was invoiced at the gross transport rate, then credited for recovered scrap value. The second record is the net replacement invoice for that collection.
The site book names two bridge decks but these entries contain neither deck name nor a receipt. The purchasing officer cannot say whether the second entry was a copy or a second collection.

The supplier made two separately paid deliveries, one to each kitchen. Both carry the overall requisition number, and their receiving locations differ.
